chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, raising it to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), said:
Rasūl Allāh (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: “O people,”

It is only Allah and the Shayṭān, and the truth and falsehood, and guidance and misguidance, and right conduct and error, and the immediate world and the Hereafter, and the final outcome, and good deeds and evil deeds.
So whatever is of good deeds belongs to Allah, and whatever is of evil deeds belongs to the Shayṭān—may Allah curse him.

key_terms.السَّيِّئَاتُ: evil deeds, acts associated with Shayṭān
key_terms.الشَّيْطَانُ: the satanic force associated with falsehood, misguidance, and evil deeds
key_terms.الضَّلَالَةُ: misguidance, straying from the right path
key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, the source of truth, guidance, and all good deeds
key_terms.الْبَاطِلُ: falsehood, that which stands opposed to truth
key_terms.الْحَسَنَاتُ: good deeds, acts attributed to Allah
key_terms.الْحَقُّ: truth, the reality aligned with Allah
key_terms.الْهُدَى: guidance, the path of divine direction

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith distinguish between what belongs to Allah and what belongs to Shayṭān?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a stark contrast between divine truth and satanic falsehood, between guidance and misguidance, and between good deeds and evil deeds. It teaches that all goodness is attributed to Allah, while evil is associated with Shayṭān, serving as a concise theological and ethical exhortation toward sincerity and right orientation.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O you people!

But rather, it is Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Satan<sup>la</sup>, and the truth and the falsehood, and the guidance and the straying, and the right way from the error, and the present and the future and the end-result, and the good deeds and the evil deeds.
So whatever was from the good deeds, so it is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and whatever was from the evil deeds, so it is for the Satans<sup>la</sup> may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse him<sup>la</sup>’.
en.sarwar: A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father in a Marfa* manner from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘O people, what there is, is Allah and Satan, Truth and falsehood, guidance and straying, wisdom and error, present and future, the consequences, the good deeds and evil deeds.
Good deeds are for Allah and evil deeds are for Satan, may Allah condemn him.’”
